subject: Capacity econ alignment: GPU benchmarking and $/1M token targets
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity econ & GPU preferences

Jordan — great talk earlier. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can size a reserved pool and give you a concrete $/1M-token estimate. Feel free to correct any numbers below.

Call summary (what you said):
- Current pilot: ~350M tokens/month (generation + chat), mostly 8–12k token long sessions for agents.
- Expected steady-state: 250–500M tokens/month; peak days up to ~1.2–1.5M tokens/day.
- Latency target: P95 <= 300ms for 256-token responses; willing to accept higher latency for very long contexts.
- Concurrency: ~15–25 concurrent request slots during peak.
- Budget range: target spend $12k–$20k/month for inference (you asked for a target $/1M tokens to use in your budget planning).
- Preference: Acme ops asked whether H100 is required or if A100 80GB reservations could hit your throughput/latency targets.

Open items for Redwood to return:
1) Recommended reserved GPU sizing (min viable + 2 scaling options)
2) Unit economics: committed $/1M tokens for A100 vs H100 reserved pools at 12- and 36-month terms
3) Expected throughput and headroom assumptions (tokens/s and concurrency) we used to price

Next steps I propose:
- We’ll run a quick GPU sizing calc and return two pricing scenarios (balanced econ vs high-throughput) by Monday.
- If those look reasonable, we’ll convert to a formal quote + capacity worksheet (attachment) and set a short follow-up call with Stephanie for benchmarking details.

Attachments I’ll include: capacity calc and a draft quote for two SKU tiers.

Cheers,
Ben

Thanks Ben — that's accurate. A couple clarifications from our side before you finalize scenarios: 

- The 350M/month is the likely first-year baseline; expecting 20–30% YoY growth. Peak days can be bursty (up to 1.5M tokens/day) when new features roll out.
- On latency: 300ms P95 for short replies is important; long-context runs can be 1–2s.
- Primary model: a 70B open model (we're validating two variants). We will rely on prefix caching for agent context where possible.

Key pricing questions for us: 
1) Please show committed $/1M-token rates for A100 80GB vs H100 (per-month reserved pools) at 12- and 36-month terms. We need the numbers so procurement can map to budget cycles.
2) For sizing: if we commit to a pool that meets 95% of peak-day demand, what headroom do we normally recommend? (We'd rather not over-commit by more than 20%.)
3) Any caveats on model compatibility / quantization that affect throughput estimates (e.g., FP16 vs 4-bit)?

Also, curious if Redwood has an uplift for enterprise support / SLA that we should budget for.

If you can get that back early next week we’ll route to procurement.

—Jordan
Jordan Liu
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity econ & GPU preferences — options and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear questions. I pulled Stephanie in for the sizing assumptions and attached the calc and a two-tier quote. High level below; see attachments for line-by-line math and token-rate assumptions.

Summary (two recommended reservation options):

1) Balanced-Econ (recommended for predictability)- Hardware: A100 80GB reserved pool- Reserved size: 4 GPUs (baseline), burst policy to add 1 extra unit of burst on demand- Estimated steady throughput: ~5k tokens/s aggregate (assumes model quantized to 4-bit where validated)- Assumed concurrency: 20 requests at 256-token median response- Unit price (committed): $22 / 1M tokens (12-month term); $18 / 1M tokens (36-month term)- Expected monthly spend (at 350M tokens): $7,700 (12m) / $6,300 (36m)

2) High-Throughput (recommended if peak handling and lowest unit cost matter)- Hardware: H100 reserved pool- Reserved size: 3 GPUs (higher per-GPU throughput compensates)- Estimated steady throughput: ~10k tokens/s aggregate (less queuing at peak)- Assumed concurrency: 25 requests at 256-token median response- Unit price (committed): $14 / 1M tokens (12-month term); $11 / 1M tokens (36-month term)- Expected monthly spend (at 350M tokens): $4,900 (12m) / $3,850 (36m)

Notes on assumptions and caveats:
- H100 yields better tokens/sec so unit cost can be lower despite higher hourly GPU cost; numbers assume our batch/kv-cache optimizations and 4-bit quantization validated for the chosen 70B variant. If quantization is not acceptable, A100 results degrade and we’ll need to re-run.
- We priced for committed reserved capacity with a 30-day baseline provisioning lead time. Burst capacity (pay-as-you-go) can be enabled for unexpected spikes; we included conservative burst costs in the PDF.
- SLA / enterprise support: 99.9% uptime SLA is an add-on; support & proactive SLA monitoring adds ~10–15% to committed spend depending on response-time band. We can include that as a line item.

Recommended next steps: 
1) Stephanie to run an A/B sizing run with your 70B trace (can do this in a 1-hr bench session). Please share a sanitized request trace (CSV) we can ingest.
2) If the bench aligns, we’ll issue a formal quote + SOW (attached) for the selected tier and term.
3) Procurement: if Acme can commit to 12 months to start, we’ll lock the 12-month unit rates and offer a 30-day right to scale up without penalty.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_calc_v2.xlsx (sizing assumptions), acme-dedicated-tier-quote.pdf (line-item pricing), SOW-draft-acme.docx

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with Stephanie if you want to walk through the calc.

Best,
